sections.h2: Where is a deed recorded in Perry County, KY?
sections.html:
Hazard is the only place to file a Perry County deed. The County Clerk's recording department sits at 481 Main Street, Suite 102, and the clerk's site publishes 606-439-0557 with Monday-to-Friday service from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon. The county's directory shows 606-436-4614 as the main clerk line. A few older pages on the clerk's site quote other hours, so confirm by phone before driving in.

Walking in is only one option. Four e-recording services are named on the clerk's land records page (Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN), and eCCLIX, the clerk's subscription index, lets attorneys, title agents and lenders read recorded instruments remotely. The clerk's FAQ says the index reaches back to 1993 and document images to 2000, so older instruments may call for a written request with a book and page.

sections.h2: What must a deed show before the Perry County Clerk accepts it?
sections.html:
The clerk's staff screen each deed, and a missing element sends it back. Kentucky clerks, Pike County's included, post the same requirements:

  • Names and mailing addresses for grantor and grantee, a legal description, and the source of title.
  • A preparation statement and a return address for the recorded original.
  • A mailing address for the next tax bill (KRS 382.135).
  • A sworn consideration statement signed by both parties before a notary, and the grantor's own notarized signature.

Gift deeds give an estimated fair cash value in place of a price. Utility-easement deeds and deeds correcting an earlier one between the same parties need no consideration statement. When a house passes by will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk before the estate closes. Quit claim deeds convey only the grantor's interest and carry no warranty of title.

sections.h2: What does the Perry County Clerk charge to record documents?
sections.html:
The clerk's schedule lists minimums by document type, and these entries come up most in a sale or an estate.

Minimum recording fees on the Perry County Clerk's fee schedule
DocumentMinimum fee
Deed$50
Deed of correction$46
Easement$50
Mortgage$80
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Power of attorney$50
Affidavit of descent$50
Will$47
Certificate of delinquency release$46

Each page after the fifth adds $3 on most entries; mortgages add $3 only after page 30. Because these are minimums, a long document costs more, and a closing agent will usually total the recording charges for the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Perry County sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. KRS 142.050 sets 50 cents on every $500 block of the price in the deed, with a partial block counted as a full one. A $91,800 deed, the Census median for owner-occupied homes here, lands at 184 blocks and a $92.00 tax. The clerk collects before recording, retains 5% for handling it, and remits the rest to the county treasurer each quarter.

  • Exempt: transfers between spouses or ex-spouses in a divorce, foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu, partitions, and tax-sale deeds.
  • Exempt: parent-to-child and grandparent-to-grandchild transfers made for nominal consideration.
  • Gifts and nominal-price deeds are measured at estimated market value instead.

A clerk who records a taxable deed without collecting can be fined $50 per offense.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes and liens at the Perry County Clerk?
sections.html:
When the sheriff's year closes on April 15, unpaid bills arrive at the clerk as certificates of delinquency and are recorded as liens on the parcels. Interest accrues monthly, commissions are added, and the county attorney sends written notice. Revenue sets the clerk's sale at no sooner than ninety days and no later than 135 days after the handover.

Perry County's clerk site points owners to a delinquent tax application, and it says eligible owners may arrange a payment plan with the county attorney. If an outside purchaser buys a certificate, the fee schedule shows $30 to record the assignment and $46 to record the release afterward. A seller carrying an open certificate should pay it, have the release recorded, and give the title company proof before closing.

sections.h2: Can Perry County Clerk staff run a title search for me?
sections.html:
No. The clerk's FAQ bars deputies from title searching, although they will help a visitor look through the books. Copy requests must be written and must carry a book and page, an instrument number, or enough particulars (borrower, lender, loan amount) to locate the paper without a search. The office keeps names of attorneys, paralegals and abstractors who produce insured title work.

The site also advertises DocAlert, a free notice service from its records software vendor. It emails an owner whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, an early warning for owners of empty or estate houses.

sections.h2: What do sellers face in the Perry County housing market?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists 26,555 residents for 2025 against 28,473 in the 2020 count. The county had 11,481 households in 2020, 29.5% of them one person living alone, with 42.0 as the median age. QuickFacts adds 2.42 people per household, 70.4% owner-occupancy, median gross rent of $798, owner costs of $1,167 with a mortgage, and median household income of $42,181.

The county spans 343 square miles along the North and Middle Forks of the Kentucky River and borders Breathitt, Knott, Letcher, Harlan, Leslie, Clay and Owsley counties. Perry County Schools run Perry County Central High School and elementary schools named East Perry, Robinson, R.W. Combs, West Perry and Viper, along with Buck School. Hazard Independent Schools cover the city with Hazard High School, Hazard Middle School and Roy G. Eversole Elementary, and Hazard Christian Academy is the private option. Hazard Community and Technical College and the Hazard ARH Regional Medical Center are the best-known institutions. Landlords and sole proprietors selling a rental or a business property should also know that the county charges a 1% occupational license tax on wages and net profit, and that anyone working inside Hazard city limits owes the county and the city.

Population history explains the vacancy numbers. Perry County grew from 11,255 residents in 1910 to 26,042 in 1920 and 42,186 in 1930, topping out at 47,828 in 1940. It then lost people in each count through 1970, when it held 26,259, rebounded to 33,763 in 1980, and has drifted down at every count since: 30,283 in 1990, 29,390 in 2000, 28,712 in 2010 and 28,473 in 2020. The 2020 census also found 13,213 housing units with 13.1% of them vacant.

Buckhorn Lake State Resort Park, on the Middle Fork, is the county's best-known recreation area, and the county holds a Kentucky Trail Town designation. Hazard and Buckhorn are the two incorporated cities, with Combs, Diablock, Jeff and part of Vicco as census-designated places. A large share of Perry County's addresses sit in named hollows and creek communities such as Ary, Bulan, Busy, Chavies, Dwarf, Happy, Typo and Viper, so ask the clerk to confirm how a parcel is indexed before searching by street address.

faqs.q: What is the address for recording a deed in Perry County?
faqs.a: 481 Main Street, Suite 102, Hazard, KY 41701. The contact block lists weekday service from eight to four.

faqs.q: What is the clerk's fee for a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars is the posted minimum, with $3 added per page beyond five. Transfer tax on the deed's stated value is a separate charge.

faqs.q: Can closing documents be recorded electronically in Perry County?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerk's land records page names Indecomm, CSC, Simplifile and ePN as e-recording services.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a Perry County deed?
faqs.a: The seller does, as grantor. Using the $91,800 Census median value, the tax comes to $92.00.

faqs.q: Will the Perry County Clerk look up my parcel's title?
faqs.a: No, staff cannot perform a title search. They can help you browse, and written copy requests need a book and page, instrument number or similar detail.
